breweries.name: Daishinsyu Shuzo
breweries.houseStyle: Mountain brewery on Japanese Alps snowmelt; cold winters for slow fermentation. Philosophy centres on respect for rice, nature and the farmer, with tight bonds to local Nagano rice growers (GI Nagano bottlings).

breweries.name: Inaba Shuzo
breweries.houseStyle: Brewing on the same plot since 1867 with Mount Tsukuba spring water. Led since 1999 by Nobuko Inaba, the 6th generation and one of very few women running a brewery at the time. Muroka/shizuku styles under the Stella label, classic Ibaraki junmai under Minanogawa.

breweries.name: Kikkawa Jozo
breweries.houseStyle: Built on the hardest natural spring water in Japan (~150 mg/L) from the Oyama-Afuri shrine area — unusual in an industry that prizes soft water. Firm, mineral, structured sake under the Afuri label.

breweries.name: Kitajima Shuzo
breweries.houseStyle: Over 200 years old; the gentle, elegant MIYOSAKAE brand for the local community and, since 2002, the rustic, region-rooted KITAJIMA brand for seasoned drinkers — kimoto, high polishing ratios, local Shiga rice.

breweries.name: Mifuku Shuzo
breweries.houseStyle: Three generations of Shiga brewing, dedicated to the Yamahai method — deep, rich, umami-and-acid driven sake built for the salty, fermented flavours of the local diet. The Sanrensei series bottles three Shiga-grown rice lineages (Wataribune Rokugo, Yamadanishiki, Ginfubuki) side by side.

breweries.name: Tanakaya Shuzo
breweries.houseStyle: Family brewery transformed from the 1990s by president Ryuta Tanaka, who traced the house style back to its water source and rebuilt quality around it. Mizuo is the flagship label.

breweries.name: Yukawa Shuzo
breweries.houseStyle: Second-oldest active brewery in Nagano, at 1,000 m altitude on the old Nakasendo road — over 370 years of brewing in one of the hardest climates in Japan. Kisoji and Kurouemon labels.
